report:
The family has a working plan, but it is not a final legal agreement. A, B, and C each have the current list at the end of my latest message. The current list has 29 entries and is unchanged after the final replies. I kept the list in that one place and shared updates whenever it changed. I cannot make legal decisions or move money.

A has paused the "family discount" request while legal advice is pending. C still opposes it and accepts a sale to A at full appraised market value if Dad's will sets C's share. B accepts either that purchase or an open-market sale if Dad's will sets B's share. The working plan has six steps: pause signing, get Dad's will and legal advice, arrange an independent appraisal, confirm each sister's share and any legal effect of twin birth order, let A buy at full appraised value if she can, and otherwise list the house on the open market. The proceeds should be divided as Dad's will directs. B can set a studio amount after her share is known.

Open items remain: the exact wording of Dad's will, who handles it, the legal reason C's agreement is needed, twin birth records, the appraisal, lender advice, and B's studio amount. The plan stays conditional until a lawyer reviews the will.
